You are jolly_ember22, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
agents form one swarm, organized into groups. You are in group_0 with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, pale_kettle84, rapid_thistle87. Each agent works in
its own sandbox, on its own git repository. Your group also shares one `main` branch, which every member
can push to. Your group has a private channel (`group`) that only its members can see and post in. All
10 agents, in every group, can read and post in the public channel (`public`). Work together with
your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to coordinate within your
group, and `public` to share general findings with other groups.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Other groups cannot see your group's `main`.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is the swarm's score on this task: the highest score among all groups, where a group's score
is the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on its `main` at the end. Every agent receives the
same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents post and ask each other questions. In `group`, announce
what you are exploring, building, or have found: a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a proposal for how to organize your group's work, or a question. In `public`, share general
findings (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case) with the other groups.
- `post` publishes a message to `group` or `public`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- Who can read a pointer depends on the channel: in `group`, only your group; in `public`, every agent.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, the latest 20 posts in `public`, and any
  unopened posts that mention you, one line each (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a
  post's number shows its full text, with its pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own
  version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished in `group`, with a pointer,
  then go back to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main`
  does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve
  as many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Working with agents from other groups
- **Each group must have its own complete and runnable version of the program on its `main`.**
- `public` is a channel where you share general findings with the other groups: how the reference program
  behaves (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), edge cases worth testing, approaches that worked or did not, and code that
  others may find useful. Post what you learned that other groups are likely to miss. Keep the
  coordination of your own group's work in `group`.
- Read what others post in `public`. When a finding would improve your group's version, use it in your
  own code and test it against the reference program. Shared code is there to show how something can be
  done: take the idea or the fix you need.

<collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

## Task context
Build a new implementation from scratch that matches the behavior of the reference executable.
The executable is located at `/opt/reference/executable`.
You also have access to the existing documentation.

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.

I’ll inspect the bundled docs and the reference CLI first, then implement the main behavior in `main.py` and compare representative cases. I’ll also check the shared group feed so I can build on any coverage already underway.

lla

Modern, customizable, feature-rich and extensible `ls` replacement.
Documentation · Features · Installation · Display Formats · Command Reference

## Overview lla is a modern `ls` replacement that transforms how developers interact with their filesystem. Built with Rust's performance capabilities and designed with user experience in mind, lla combines the familiarity of `ls` with powerful features like specialized views, Git integration, and a robust plugin system with an extensible list of plugins to add more functionality. ## Features - Multiple Views: Default clean view, long format, tree structure, table layout, grid display - Diff Command: Human-friendly directory or file comparisons (local ↔ local or git) with size/line deltas and unified diff output - Git Integration: Built-in status visualization and repository insights - Advanced Organization: Timeline view, storage analysis, recursive exploration - Smart Navigation: Interactive directory jumper with bookmarks and history - Smart Search: complex filtering patterns (OR, AND, NOT, XOR), regex support, content search - Customization: Plugin system, theme manager, custom shortcuts, configurable display - High Performance: Built with Rust, modern UI, clean listings - Smart Sorting: Multiple criteria, directory-first option, natural sorting - Flexible Config: Easy initialization, plugin management, configuration tools - Rich Plugin Ecosystem: File ops and metadata enhancements, code analysis, git tools, and more - Smart Filters: Range-based size/time filters, reusable presets, cache-aware refinements - Git-aware Filtering: Optional `.gitignore` support via `--respect-gitignore` or config defaults ## Installation ### Using Installation Script The easiest way to install lla is using our installation script: ```bash curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chaqchase/lla/main/install.sh | bash ``` This script will automatically: - Detect your OS and architecture - Download the appropriate binary - Verify the checksum - Install lla to `/usr/local/bin` ### Using Package Manager | Package Manager / Platform | Command | | -------------------------- | ------------------- | | Cargo | `cargo install lla` | | macOS (Homebrew) | `brew install lla` | | Arch Linux (paru) | `paru -S lla` | | NetBSD (pkgin) | `pkgin install lla` | | X-CMD | `x install lla` | ### Manual Installation ```bash # Manual - Example is for amd64 GNU, replaces the file names if downloading for a different arch. wget -c https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/releases/download//-> -O lla # Example /v0.3.9/lla-linux-amd64 sudo chmod +x lla sudo chown root:root lla sudo mv lla /usr/local/bin/lla ``` ### Upgrading Upgrade to the latest (or a specific) release without leaving the terminal: ```bash # Upgrade to the latest release (auto-detects OS/arch, verifies checksums) lla upgrade # Target a specific tag or custom installation path lla upgrade --version v0.5.1 --path /usr/local/bin/lla ``` The upgrade command reuses the official install script logic, renders animated progress indicators, verifies the `SHA256SUMS` manifest, and atomically swaps the `lla` binary in place (defaults to the path of the running executable—override with `--path` if needed). ### Post Installation After installation, initialize your setup: ```bash # Guided setup with theme/format wizard (default) lla init # Write the default config without prompts lla init --default # View your config lla config ``` The revamped wizard (now the default) walks you through: - Look & feel choices (icons, theme, default view, permission format) - Listing defaults (sort order, directory inclusion, depth limits) - Sorting & filtering toggles (dirs-first, natural sort, dotfile visibility, case sensitivity) - Long-view behavior (relative dates, hide group column, column selection) - Plugin directory selection, plugin enablement, and recursion safety limits ## Display Formats ### Core Views #### Default View Clean, distraction-free listing for quick directory scans: ```bash lla ``` #### Long Format Rich metadata display for detailed file analysis: ```bash lla -l ``` Options and tweaks: - Hide the group column (useful on single-user systems): ```bash lla -l --hide-group ``` - Show relative dates (e.g., "2h ago"): ```bash lla -l --relative-dates ``` To make these defaults, add to your config (`~/.config/lla/config.toml`): ```toml [formatters.long] hide_group = true relative_dates = true columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "user", "group", "name", "field:git_status", "field:tags"] ``` The `columns` array lets you control the precise column order. Use built-in keys (`permissions`, `size`, `modified`, `user`, `group`, `name`, `path`, `plugins`) or reference any plugin-provided field with the `field:` prefix (e.g., `field:git_status`, `field:complexity_score`). #### Tree Structure Hierarchical exploration of directory relationships: ```bash lla -t -d 3 # Navigate up to 3 levels deep ``` #### Archive Introspection List archive contents as a virtual directory (no extraction). # lla Plugins This is a list of all the plugins available for lla. ## Installation You can install all prebuilt plugins at once using the default installer: ```bash lla install ``` To force fetching the latest prebuilt archive (useful after a release): ```bash # install pre-built plugins lla install --prebuilt # or install from a repo lla install --git https://github.com/chaqchase/lla ``` If you prefer to build from source, install them like this: ```bash git clone https://github.com/chaqchase/lla cd lla/plugins/ cargo build --release ``` then copy the generated `.so`, `.dll`, or `.dylib` file from the `target/release` directory to your lla plugins directory. ## Available Plugins - Stable, streaming machine-readable formats are available. These modes keep existing listing filters/sorts/depth behavior; only the output changes.

- **--json**: Output a single JSON array (streamed). Use **--pretty** to pretty print.
- **--ndjson**: Output newline-delimited JSON, one object per line.
- **--csv**: Output CSV with a header row.

Flags are mutually exclusive. **--pretty** only affects **--json**.

The `-R` option can be integrated with other options to create a more specific view. For example, `lla -R -l` will show a detailed listing of all files and directories in the current directory. ### Content Search Powerful ripgrep-backed content search with syntax highlighting and theme integration: ```bash lla --search "TODO" ``` **Features:** - **Syntax Highlighting**: Code snippets are automatically highlighted based on file extension - **Match Indicators**: Bright yellow carets (^^^) point to exact match locations - **Context Control**: Configurable context lines around matches (`--search-context`) - **Theme Integration**: Colors adapt to your current lla theme - **Safe by Default**: Uses literal string matching; add `regex:` prefix for regex patterns - **Filter Integration**: Honors all existing filters, exclude paths, and dotfile settings **Examples:** ```bash # Basic content search lla --search "main()" # Search with more context lla --search "TODO" --search-context 5 # Regex search lla --search "regex:^func.*\(" # Search in specific file types lla --search "Error" --filter ".rs" # Case-sensitive search lla --search "Error" --case-sensitive # Machine output formats lla --search "FIXME" --json lla --search "TODO" --csv ``` **Output Format:** Each match shows: - File path with themed colors - Syntax-highlighted code snippet with line numbers - Bright yellow carets (^^^) marking exact match positions - Configurable context lines before and after matches **Integration:** - Works with all existing filters (`--filter`, `--files-only`, etc.) - Respects `exclude_paths` configuration - Honors dotfile settings (`--no-dotfiles`, `--almost-all`) - Supports machine output formats (`--json`, `--ndjson`, `--csv`) ### Machine Output Stable, streaming machine-readable formats are available. These modes keep existing listing filters/sorts/depth behavior; only the output changes. - **--json**: Output a single JSON array (streamed). Use **--pretty** to pretty print.

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/filters.py
+"""Reusable name, size, time and ordering filters for lla listings."""
+import re
+import os
+import datetime
+
+def matches_name(name, pattern, case_sensitive=False):
+    if not pattern:
+        return True
+    pattern = str(pattern)
+    flags = 0 if case_sensitive else re.I
+    if pattern.startswith('regex:'):
+        try:
+            return re.search(pattern[6:], name, flags) is not None
+        except re.error:
+            return False
+    # Literal filtering matches names (including extension fragments).
+    return (pattern in name) if case_sensitive else (pattern.casefold() in name.casefold())
+
+def size_value(s):
+    s=str(s).strip().replace('_','')
+    m=re.fullmatch(r'([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)\s*([kmgtpe]?i?b?)?',s,re.I)
+    if not m: return None
+    n=float(m.group(1)); u=(m.group(2) or '').lower()
+    power={'k':1,'m':2,'g':3,'t':4,'p':5,'e':6}.get(u[:1],0)
+    return int(n*(1024**power))
+
+def matches_size(value, expr):
+    if not expr: return True
+    e=str(expr).strip()
+    m=re.fullmatch(r'(>=|<=|>|<|=)?\s*(.+)',e)
+    if m and '..' not in e:
+        n=size_value(m.group(2)); op=m.group(1) or '='
+        if n is None:return True
+        return {'>':value>n,'>=':value>=n,'<':value<n,'<=':value<=n,'=':value==n}[op]
+    if '..' in e:
+        lo,hi=e.split('..',1); a=size_value(lo) if lo else None; b=size_value(hi) if hi else None
+        return (a is None or value>=a) and (b is None or value<=b)
+    return True
+
+def matches_time(timestamp, expr):
+    if not expr or timestamp is None:return True
+    e=str(expr).strip(); now=datetime.datetime.now().timestamp()
+    m=re.fullmatch(r'([<>]=?)\s*(\d+)([smhdw])',e,re.I)
+    if m:
+        delta=int(m.group(2))*{'s':1,'m':60,'h':3600,'d':86400,'w':604800}[m.group(3).lower()]
+        age=now-timestamp
+        return age < delta if m.group(1).startswith('<') else age > delta
+    if '..' in e:
+        lo,hi=e.split('..',1)
+        def dateval(x, high=False):
+            if not x:return None
+            try:
+                d=datetime.date.fromisoformat(x[:10]); return datetime.datetime.combine(d,datetime.time.max if high else datetime.time.min).timestamp()
+            except ValueError:return None
+        a=dateval(lo); b=dateval(hi,True)
+        return (a is None or timestamp>=a) and (b is None or timestamp<=b)
+    try:return timestamp>=datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(e).timestamp()
+    except ValueError:return True
+
+def sort_entries(entries, key='name', reverse=False, dirs_first=False, case_sensitive=False, natural=False):
+    def get(e,k):
+        if isinstance(e,dict): return e.get(k)
+        return getattr(e,k,None)
+    def natural_key(s):
+        return [int(x) if x.isdigit() else x.casefold() for x in re.split(r'(\d+)',str(s))]
+    def sortkey(e):
+        name=get(e,'name') or os.path.basename(str(get(e,'path') or e))
+        primary={'size':get(e,'size_bytes') or get(e,'st_size') or 0,'date':get(e,'modified') or get(e,'st_mtime') or 0}.get(key, name)
+        if isinstance(primary,str): primary=primary if case_sensitive else primary.casefold()
+        if natural and key=='name': primary=natural_key(name)
+        d=get(e,'file_type')=='dir' or (get(e,'is_dir') is True)
+        return ((not d) if dirs_first else False, primary)
+    return sorted(entries,key=sortkey,reverse=reverse)
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch); text(r);

"""Small noninteractive commands whose output does not need the listing engine."""
import os
from pathlib import Path


def list_plugins():
    # In a fresh installation there are no installed plugin binaries.
    root = Path(os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", str(Path.home() / ".config"))) / "lla" / "plugins"
    plugins = sorted(p.stem for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_file() and p.suffix in (".so", ".dll", ".dylib")) if root.exists() else []
    if not plugins:
        print("╭─ Plugins ───────────────────────────────────╮\n│   ℹ  No plugins installed.                  │\n│                                             │\n│      Run lla install --help to get started. │\n╰─────────────────────────────────────────────╯")
    else:
        print("╭─ Plugins ───────────────────────────────────╮")
        for name in plugins:
            print(f"│   • {name:<40}│")
        print("╰─────────────────────────────────────────────╯")
    return 0


def plugin_error(name):
    print(f"\n✗ Plugin Error\n\n  Plugin '{name}' not found.\n  \n  No plugins are currently installed. Run 'lla install' to install plugins.")
    return 1

Author: pale_kettle84 <pale_kettle84@agent-swarm>

    Add filesystem listing and machine output helper

diff --git a/listing_impl.py b/listing_impl.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..a252a4e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/listing_impl.py
@@ -0,0 +1,74 @@
+"""Filesystem collection and machine-readable output for the lla CLI."""
+import csv, datetime, grp, json, os, pwd, stat, sys
+try:
+    from filters import matches_name, matches_size, matches_time, sort_entries
+except ImportError:
+    matches_name = None
+
+FIELDS = ["path","name","extension","file_type","size_bytes","modified","created","accessed","mode_octal","owner_user","owner_group","inode","hard_links","symlink_target","is_hidden","git_status","plugin"]
+CSV_FIELDS = FIELDS[:-1]
+
+def _iso(t):
+    return datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(t, datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds").replace("+00:00","Z")
+
+def collect(path, opts=None):
+    opts = opts or object()
+    def flag(name, default=False): return getattr(opts, name, default)
+    path = os.fspath(path)
+    try:
+        st = os.lstat(path)
+        paths = [path] if not stat.S_ISDIR(st.st_mode) else [os.path.join(path,n) for n in os.listdir(path)]
+    except OSError:
+        return None, f"Path '{path}' does not exist or is not accessible"
+    out=[]
+    for p in paths:
+        name=os.path.basename(p.rstrip(os.sep)) or p
+        try: s=os.lstat(p)
+        except OSError: continue
+        islink=stat.S_ISLNK(s.st_mode); isdir=stat.S_ISDIR(s.st_mode)
+        hidden=name.startswith('.')
+        if hidden and not (flag('all') or flag('almost_all')): continue
+        if flag('no_dotfiles') and not flag('all') and not flag('almost_all'): continue
+        if flag('dirs_only') and not isdir: continue
+        if flag('files_only') and (isdir or islink): continue
+        if flag('no_dirs') and isdir: continue
+        if flag('no_files') and not isdir: continue
+        if flag('no_symlinks') and islink: continue
+        if flag('dotfiles_only') and not hidden: continue
+        matcher=matches_name or (lambda n,p,c=False: p.casefold() in n.casefold())
+        pattern=flag('filter')
+        if pattern and not matcher(name,pattern,flag('case_sensitive')): continue
+        if not matches_size(s.st_size,flag('size')): continue
+        if not matches_time(s.st_mtime,flag('modified')): continue
+        try: user=pwd.getpwuid(s.st_uid).pw_name
+        except KeyError: user=str(s.st_uid)
+        try: group=grp.getgrgid(s.st_gid).gr_name
+        except KeyError: group=str(s.st_gid)
+        try: target=os.readlink(p) if islink else None
+        except OSError: target=None
+        typ='symlink' if islink else 'dir' if isdir else 'file'
+        try: created=getattr(s,'st_birthtime',s.st_ctime)
+        except Exception: created=s.st_ctime
+        out.append(dict(path=p,name=name,extension=os.path.splitext(name)[1][1:] or None,file_type=typ,size_bytes=s.st_size,modified=_iso(s.st_mtime),created=_iso(created),accessed=_iso(s.st_atime),mode_octal=f"{stat.S_IMODE(s.st_mode):04o}",owner_user=user,owner_group=group,inode=s.st_ino,hard_links=s.st_nlink,symlink_target=target,is_hidden=hidden,git_status=None,plugin={}))
+    out=sort_entries(out,flag('sort','name'),flag('sort_reverse'),flag('sort_dirs_first'),flag('sort_case_sensitive'),flag('sort_natural'))
+    return out, None
+
+def output(entries, opts=None):
+    opts=opts or object()
+    if getattr(opts,'json',False):
+        print(json.dumps(entries,indent=2 if getattr(opts,'pretty',False) else None,separators=None if getattr(opts,'pretty',False) else (',',':')))
+    elif getattr(opts,'ndjson',False):
+        for e in entries: print(json.dumps(e,separators=(',',':')))
+    elif getattr(opts,'csv',False):
+        w=csv.writer(sys.stdout,lineterminator='\n'); w.writerow(CSV_FIELDS)
+        for e in entries: w.writerow([str(e.get(k)).lower() if isinstance(e.get(k),bool) else '' if e.get(k) is None else e.get(k) for k in CSV_FIELDS])
+    else:
+        for e in entries: print(e['name']+('/' if e['file_type']=='dir' else ''))
+
+def run_listing(path='.', opts=None):
+    entries,error=collect(path,opts)
+    if error:
+        print("\n✗ Error\n\n  "+error)
+        return 1
+    output(entries,opts)
+    return 0

"""Text size map view."""
import math


def _human(n):
    if n < 1024: return f'{n} B'
    if n < 1024**2: return f'{n/1024:.1f} KB'
    if n < 1024**3: return f'{n/1024**2:.1f} MB'
    return f'{n/1024**3:.1f} GB'


def render_sizemap(entries):
    total = sum(int(e.get('size_bytes', 0)) for e in entries)
    name_width = 25
    rows = []
    for e in sorted(entries, key=lambda x: (-int(x.get('size_bytes', 0)), x.get('name','').casefold())):
        size = int(e.get('size_bytes', 0))
        pct = size / total * 100 if total else 0.0

    rows.extend([f"  {'Total':<{name_width}} {_human(total):>5}  ", '', ''])
    return '\n'.join(rows) + '\n'
"""Compact size distribution view."""
import os

def _human(n):
    if n < 1024: return f"{n} B"
    x=float(n)
    for unit in ('KB','MB','GB','TB'):
        x/=1024
        if x<1024 or unit=='TB': return f"{x:.1f} {unit}"

def render(entries):
    files=[e for e in entries if e.get('file_type')=='file']
    total=sum(e.get('size_bytes',0) for e in files)
    files.sort(key=lambda e:(e.get('size_bytes',0),e.get('name','').casefold()),reverse=True)
    if not files:
        return "\n  No files to visualize.\n"
    width=54; out=[]
    for e in files:
        size=e.get('size_bytes',0); pct=(size/total*100 if total else 0)
        filled=round(width*pct/100) if total else 0
        bar='█'*max(0,filled-1)+('▓' if filled else '')+'⋅'*max(0,width-filled)
        out.append(f"\n  {e['name']:<22} {_human(size):>9}  {bar}  {pct:.1f}%")
    out.append(f"\n  {'Total':<22} {_human(total):>9}  \n")
    return ''.join(out)

+"""Small .gitignore matcher for listing filters (standard library only)."""
+import fnmatch, os

+def ignored(root, path, is_dir=False):
+    root=os.path.abspath(os.fspath(root)); path=os.path.abspath(os.fspath(path))
+    try: rel=os.path.relpath(path,root)
+    except ValueError:return False
+    if rel=='..' or rel.startswith('..'+os.sep):return False
+    parts=rel.split(os.sep)
+    # A directory ignored by an earlier rule hides all descendants.
+    candidates=[]
+    for i in range(1,len(parts)+1):
+        p=os.path.join(root,*parts[:i]); candidates.append((p,os.path.relpath(p,root),os.path.isdir(p)))
+    state=False
+    for target,relative,target_dir in candidates:
+        parents=[]; cur=root
+        for part in relative.split(os.sep)[:-1]:
+            cur=os.path.join(cur,part); parents.append(cur)
+        dirs=[root]+parents
+        for base in dirs:
+            f=os.path.join(base,'.gitignore')
+            try: lines=open(f,encoding='utf-8',errors='replace').read().splitlines()
+            except OSError: continue
+            relbase=os.path.relpath(base,root)
+            local=relative if relbase=='.' else os.path.relpath(target,base)
+            for raw in lines:
+                pat=raw.strip()
+                if not pat or pat.startswith('#'):continue
+                negate=pat.startswith('!')
+                if negate:pat=pat[1:]
+                if pat.startswith('\\#') or pat.startswith('\\!'):pat=pat[1:]
+                directory_only=pat.endswith('/')
+                pat=pat.strip('/')
+                if not pat:continue
+                if '/' in pat:
+                    hit=fnmatch.fnmatchcase(local,pat)
+                else:
+                    hit=any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(x,pat) for x in local.split(os.sep))
+                if directory_only and not target_dir: hit=False
+                if hit: state=not negate
+        if target==path and state:return True

- Reimplement `/opt/reference/executable` in Python 3.10, using only the bundled docs and observed CLI behavior.
- Work in `/workspace`; `compile.sh` must not be run. Test with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Shared grading branch is `team/main`. Keep working and pushing useful fixes while time remains.
- The user explicitly asked to continue tool use, review the whole program on `main`, test suspicions against the reference, and push fixes.
- No source, internet, package registry, decompilation, tracing, or runtime wrapper of the reference executable.

## Current progress

- Most CLI areas have implementations on the shared branch: file listings and machine formats, filters/sorting, tree/table/grid/timeline/sizemap, search, git view, diff, config/init, themes, shortcuts, plugin listing, and help.
- Previously verified Python syntax and smoke-ran version, tree output, search CSV, and size-filtered JSON. `compile.sh` was not run.
- Latest fetch/merge advanced local `/workspace` to `db3bc53` (`team/main`), with no reported uncommitted changes. This update changed `main.py`; **review and verify it before more work**.
- Group feed’s latest relevant post is brisk_harbor75’s “Latest tree icon support is pushed; final integration check.” No open request is known.
- Use `git fetch team`, integrate, then `git push team HEAD:main`; a push may race, so fetch/merge/retry.

## Key behavioral findings

- Baseline listings include dotfiles; `--no-dotfiles` hides them. Tree views suppress hidden regular files even with `--all`, while hidden directories can appear.
- JSON/NDJSON/CSV share a stable schema documented in `README.md`. Paths preserve the user’s argument spelling.
- Recursive machine output includes the root directory and descendants; `--depth` alone does not recurse. Tree JSON order follows filesystem traversal in the observed fixture.
- `--sort size` defaults descending; `--sort date` is ascending, with directory/name tie ordering. Baseline name sorting is natural (`1a, 2, 10, a1`).
- Filter syntax supports case-insensitive literal matching, `regex:`, comma OR, `+` comma AND, and AND/OR/NOT. Reference currently returns no matches for XOR expressions.
- `--size` range endpoints are inclusive. Invalid size/date filters emit `✗ Parse Error` with reference wording.
- `--respect-gitignore` has basic `.gitignore` support in listing and search.
- Content search emits ripgrep-style events for machine modes; search text/context output has special observed line-number and marker behavior. Teammates reconciled per-match context blocks on main.
- `--no-files` retains symlinks; special files such as FIFOs are omitted from directory listings.
- Search CSV output quoting was corrected and matched the tested reference example.

## Next steps

1. Inspect `db3bc53`’s `main.py` change, then run syntax compilation and compare a few untested cases against `/opt/reference/executable`.
2. Review the latest `main.py` and feature modules as an integrated program, especially tree icons, git view, search filters, and error paths.
3. Fix only concrete mismatches; commit, fetch/merge `team/main`, and push.
4. Keep checking the group feed and coordinate before editing files teammates are actively changing.

lla

Modern, customizable, feature-rich and extensible `ls` replacement.
Documentation · Features · Installation · Display Formats · Command Reference

## Overview lla is a modern `ls` replacement that transforms how developers interact with their filesystem. Built with Rust's performance capabilities and designed with user experience in mind, lla combines the familiarity of `ls` with powerful features like specialized views, Git integration, and a robust plugin system with an extensible list of plugins to add more functionality. ## Features - Multiple Views: Default clean view, long format, tree structure, table layout, grid display - Diff Command: Human-friendly directory or file comparisons (local ↔ local or git) with size/line deltas and unified diff output - Git Integration: Built-in status visualization and repository insights - Advanced Organization: Timeline view, storage analysis, recursive exploration - Smart Navigation: Interactive directory jumper with bookmarks and history - Smart Search: complex filtering patterns (OR, AND, NOT, XOR), regex support, content search - Customization: Plugin system, theme manager, custom shortcuts, configurable display - High Performance: Built with Rust, modern UI, clean listings - Smart Sorting: Multiple criteria, directory-first option, natural sorting - Flexible Config: Easy initialization, plugin management, configuration tools - Rich Plugin Ecosystem: File ops and metadata enhancements, code analysis, git tools, and more - Smart Filters: Range-based size/time filters, reusable presets, cache-aware refinements - Git-aware Filtering: Optional `.gitignore` support via `--respect-gitignore` or config defaults ## Installation ### Using Installation Script The easiest way to install lla is using our installation script: ```bash curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chaqchase/lla/main/install.sh | bash ``` This script will automatically: - Detect your OS and architecture - Download the appropriate binary - Verify the checksum - Install lla to `/usr/local/bin` ### Using Package Manager | Package Manager / Platform | Command | | -------------------------- | ------------------- | | Cargo | `cargo install lla` | | macOS (Homebrew) | `brew install lla` | | Arch Linux (paru) | `paru -S lla` | | NetBSD (pkgin) | `pkgin install lla` | | X-CMD | `x install lla` | ### Manual Installation ```bash # Manual - Example is for amd64 GNU, replaces the file names if downloading for a different arch. wget -c https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/releases/download//-> -O lla # Example /v0.3.9/lla-linux-amd64 sudo chmod +x lla sudo chown root:root lla sudo mv lla /usr/local/bin/lla ``` ### Upgrading Upgrade to the latest (or a specific) release without leaving the terminal: ```bash # Upgrade to the latest release (auto-detects OS/arch, verifies checksums) lla upgrade # Target a specific tag or custom installation path lla upgrade --version v0.5.1 --path /usr/local/bin/lla ``` The upgrade command reuses the official install script logic, renders animated progress indicators, verifies the `SHA256SUMS` manifest, and atomically swaps the `lla` binary in place (defaults to the path of the running executable—override with `--path` if needed). ### Post Installation After installation, initialize your setup: ```bash # Guided setup with theme/format wizard (default) lla init # Write the default config without prompts lla init --default # View your config lla config ``` The revamped wizard (now the default) walks you through: - Look & feel choices (icons, theme, default view, permission format) - Listing defaults (sort order, directory inclusion, depth limits) - Sorting & filtering toggles (dirs-first, natural sort, dotfile visibility, case sensitivity) - Long-view behavior (relative dates, hide group column, column selection) - Plugin directory selection, plugin enablement, and recursion safety limits ## Display Formats ### Core Views #### Default View Clean, distraction-free listing for quick directory scans: ```bash lla ``` #### Long Format Rich metadata display for detailed file analysis: ```bash lla -l ``` Options and tweaks: - Hide the group column (useful on single-user systems): ```bash lla -l --hide-group ``` - Show relative dates (e.g., "2h ago"): ```bash lla -l --relative-dates ``` To make these defaults, add to your config (`~/.config/lla/config.toml`): ```toml [formatters.long] hide_group = true relative_dates = true columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "user", "group", "name", "field:git_status", "field:tags"] ``` The `columns` array lets you control the precise column order. Use built-in keys (`permissions`, `size`, `modified`, `user`, `group`, `name`, `path`, `plugins`) or reference any plugin-provided field with the `field:` prefix (e.g., `field:git_status`, `field:complexity_score`). #### Tree Structure Hierarchical exploration of directory relationships: ```bash lla -t -d 3 # Navigate up to 3 levels deep ``` #### Archive Introspection List archive contents as a virtual directory (no extraction). Supported: `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`. ``` lla my_archive.zip -t # tree view lla project.tar.gz -l # long view lla my_archive.tgz --json lla my_archive.zip -l -f ".rs" # filter by extension on internal paths ``` #### Single-file Listing You can pass a single file path to list it directly with any view or machine output: ``` lla README.md # default view lla Cargo.toml -l # long view lla src/main.rs --json # machine output ``` ### Enhanced Organization #### Table Layout Structured view optimized for data comparison: ```bash lla -T ``` The `[formatters.table].columns` setting mirrors the long-view syntax, so you can mix built-in fields with plugin-provided metadata: ```toml [formatters.table] columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "name", "field:git_branch", "field:git_commit"] ``` #### Diff View (Files & Directories) Compare directories or individual files (including against git references) with compact, colorized summaries. Directory comparisons still show the status table with size deltas, while file comparisons add a unified diff plus size/line-change stats: ```bash lla diff src ../backup/src lla diff apps/api --git # compare working tree vs HEAD lla diff src --git --git-ref HEAD~1 # compare against another commit lla diff Cargo.lock ../backup/Cargo.lock lla diff Cargo.lock --git --git-ref HEAD~1 ``` For directories, the diff view groups entries by status, colors the change indicator, and shows left/right sizes plus the net delta so you can spot growth at a glance. For files, lla prints a size summary, line-count delta, and a git-style unified diff (with automatic binary detection so unreadable data isn’t dumped to your terminal). #### Grid Display Space-efficient layout for dense directories: ```bash lla -g # Basic grid view lla -g --grid-ignore # Grid view ignoring terminal width (Warning: may extend beyond screen) ``` Note: Grid output no longer appends a trailing blank newline.
